title: Whipped Cream
description: Cold heavy cream whipped with a little sugar and vanilla to medium peaks.
beforeYouStart: Keep the cream in the fridge until you need it. Cold cream whips best.
Set out a large bowl and a hand or stand mixer with the whisk.

steps.do: Whip the cream, sugar and vanilla on medium-high speed to medium peaks, about 3 to 4 minutes. If it goes too far and looks curdled and heavy, fold in a splash more cold cream by hand until it smooths out.
steps.cue: Medium peaks: firmer than soft, not yet stiff

steps.do: Use right away, or cover tightly and refrigerate up to 24 hours.

notes: Use heavy cream or heavy whipping cream. Plain whipping cream has less fat and won't hold its shape as long; half-and-half and milk won't whip.
Cream doubles in volume as it whips, so 1 cup makes about 2 cups. The recipe doubles or triples easily.
Sugar: at this amount, granulated and confectioners' work the same. In bigger batches granulated can taste gritty, so use confectioners'. Brown sugar works too.
Freezing: freeze in a container, or in dollops on a parchment-lined sheet and then bag them, up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge. It's a little less creamy after thawing.
